text:
Ivy (Docs): Pushed a draft to expand the Dedicated provisioning guide with a short quantization guidance section + isolation tier clarifications. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2678
Marco (ML Eng): Nice. A few quick cautions: int8/static quant can change memory layout and KV-cache hit characteristics. Recommend calling out `quantize_mode: \"dynamic\"` for small GPUs to reduce first-request regressions.
Luis (SDK): Also noticing some snippets still use `batch_size` in examples. Our public SDK param is `batch_limit` now. Can we normalize both Python and JS snippets?
Ivy (Docs): Good catch, will replace `batch_size` -> `batch_limit` everywhere. Adding a one-line callout: "Use conservative batch_limit on small on-prem pools."
Hannah (Security): Please include a short note about key management: Dedicated Private deployments should reference KMS/HSM integration and audit log locations. Our internal link used to be /internal/security/kms.
ops-bot: Link check failed: /internal/security/kms -> 404 (found in docs/dedicated/security.md line ~24)
Ivy (Docs): Fixed the link to /security/key-management and added a brief bullet: "Private Dedicated: integrate with your KMS/HSM and enable audit logs for inference requests."
Marco (ML Eng): For terraform examples, suggest adding vars: `default_quant_mode = \"dynamic\"` and `default_batch_limit = 3` (good starting point for small 1-2 GPU pools).
Luis (SDK): I pushed a tiny SDK snippet suggestion for the PR description. Examples should be runnable:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-dedicated-1', prompt='Hello', batch_limit=3, quantizeMode='dynamic')
print(resp.text)
```
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-dedicated-1', prompt: 'Hello', batch_limit: 3, quantizeMode: 'dynamic' })
console.log(res.text)
```
Ivy (Docs): Added the SDK snippets, terraform var examples, and a short warmup note: "First few requests may show higher latency while KV caches warm; consider small prewarm pools for tail-sensitive workloads."
ops-bot: CI checks passed for PR #2678 (link-check, lint).
Ivy (Docs): Merged after green CI. Filed follow-up issue #534 to add a small perf table (cold vs warm median latencies for 128/512 tokens) and to enroll the new snippets in docs-smoke.
Marco (ML Eng): Thanks 51; will add perf numbers to issue #534 once we run the benchmark on the mixed-quant setup.
